node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Angle as turn
node.description: Understand an angle as the amount of turn between two rays or directions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare and estimate angles
node.description: Compare angle sizes and estimate angles using benchmark turns and degrees.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Classify angles
node.description: Classify angles as acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex or full turn.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Degrees as angle units
node.description: Use degrees as standard units for measuring angle size.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Measure angles with protractor
node.description: Use a protractor to measure angles accurately in degrees.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Construct angles with protractor
node.description: Construct angles of specified sizes using a protractor and ruler.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Reflex angles
node.description: Measure and reason about angles greater than 180 degrees and less than 360 degrees.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Angle notation
node.description: Name and represent angles using symbols, vertex notation and diagrams.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Angles on a straight line
node.description: Use the fact that adjacent angles on a straight line sum to 180 degrees.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Complementary and supplementary angles
node.description: Identify and use complementary and supplementary angle relationships.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Angles around a point

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Vertically opposite angles
node.description: Recognise and use equality of vertically opposite angles formed by intersecting lines.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Triangle angle sum

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Quadrilateral angle sum

node.subject: Mathematics

node.subject: Mathematics

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Angle is amount of turn
node.description: An angle measures the amount of turn between two rays or directions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Protractor uses centre and baseline
node.description: Accurate protractor measurement requires placing the centre and baseline correctly.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Angle benchmarks support estimation
node.description: Right, straight and full-turn angles provide benchmarks for estimating angle size.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Straight line is 180 degrees
node.description: Adjacent angles on a straight line sum to 180 degrees.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Full turn is 360 degrees
node.description: Angles around a point make a full turn of 360 degrees.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Triangle angles sum to 180 degrees
node.description: The interior angles of a triangle sum to 180 degrees.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Parallel lines create angle pairs
node.description: Parallel lines cut by a transversal create corresponding, alternate and co-interior angle relationships.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Opposite and adjacent depend on angle
node.description: Opposite and adjacent side names depend on which acute angle is chosen, while the hypotenuse is opposite the right angle.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Trigonometric ratios link sides and angles
node.description: Sine, cosine and tangent connect acute angle size to ratios of right-triangle side lengths.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Inverse trigonometry finds angles

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Angle size depends on side length
node.description: Learner thinks longer drawn arms make a larger angle even when the turn is unchanged.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Use wrong protractor scale
node.description: Learner reads the incorrect protractor scale or ignores the baseline direction.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Reflex angle read as acute
node.description: Learner reports only the smaller angle when the intended angle is reflex.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Parallel angle pair confusion
node.description: Learner misidentifies corresponding, alternate or co-interior angle relationships in parallel-line diagrams.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Hypotenuse has fixed diagram position
node.description: Learner identifies the hypotenuse by visual position rather than as the side opposite the right angle.

edge.rationale: Angle-as-turn is foundational to angle measurement.
Comparing and estimating angle size directly practises angle measure.
Classifying angles is a core application of angle-size benchmarks.
Degrees are the standard unit for this angle-measure progression.
Protractor measurement directly practises measuring angles in degrees.
Constructing specified angles applies angle measurement in reverse.
Reflex angles extend angle measurement beyond 180 degrees.
Angle notation supports communicating measured and unknown angles.
Straight-line angle sums are core angle relationships.
Complementary and supplementary relationships are core angle-sum cases.
Angles around a point extend sum reasoning to a full turn.
Vertically opposite angles are a standard line-intersection relationship.
Triangle angle sum is a major geometric angle relationship.
Quadrilateral angle sum extends triangle-sum reasoning.
Parallel-line relationships are central to angle reasoning in diagrams.
Multi-step angle chasing applies several angle relationships together.
Side names are required for using right-triangle trigonometric ratios.
Sine, cosine and tangent ratios are the core content of right-triangle trigonometry.
Choosing the appropriate ratio is central to solving right-triangle problems.
Finding missing sides is a core right-triangle trigonometry application.
Finding missing angles applies inverse trigonometric reasoning.
Angle as turn builds on spatial direction and position language.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot describe a turn or orientation change between directions.

edge.rationale: Comparing angle size requires recognising angles as amounts of turn.
edge.failure_signal: Learner compares side length instead of turn size.

edge.rationale: Angle classification depends on comparing angles with benchmark sizes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot distinguish acute, right and obtuse angles reliably.

edge.rationale: Degrees quantify angle size as amount of turn.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats degree measure as side length or unrelated labels.

edge.rationale: Protractor measurement requires using degrees as angle units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads marks without relating them to degree measure.

edge.rationale: Constructing angles with a protractor reverses the measuring process.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot align the baseline or mark the intended degree size.

edge.rationale: Reflex angles extend angle classification beyond straight angles.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reports the smaller angle rather than the reflex angle.

edge.rationale: Angle notation is usually introduced alongside measured and unknown angles, though it can be taught earlier.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify which angle is named by a vertex or symbol.

edge.rationale: Straight-line angle sums require knowing degree measure and the 180-degree straight angle benchmark.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot use 180 degrees as the total on a straight line.

edge.rationale: Supplementary angle reasoning builds directly from straight-line angle sums.
edge.failure_signal: Learner confuses complementary and supplementary totals.

edge.rationale: Angles around a point extend straight-line angle-sum reasoning to a full turn.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses 180 degrees instead of 360 degrees around a point.

edge.rationale: Vertically opposite angle equality can be reasoned from straight-line supplementary pairs.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats adjacent and vertically opposite angles as interchangeable.

edge.rationale: Triangle angle sum can be reasoned from straight-line and parallel-line relationships.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot use 180 degrees as the total for triangle interior angles.

edge.rationale: Quadrilateral angle sum can be decomposed into two triangle angle sums.
edge.failure_signal: Learner does not connect quadrilateral angle total to two triangles.

edge.rationale: Parallel-line angle reasoning builds on line-intersection angle relationships.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify equal or supplementary angle pairs in line diagrams.

edge.rationale: Multi-step angle chasing combines parallel-line, triangle and straight-line relationships.
edge.failure_signal: Learner applies one relationship but cannot chain multiple relationships.

edge.rationale: Right-triangle side naming depends on recognising right angles and chosen acute angles in triangles.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify hypotenuse, opposite and adjacent sides relative to an angle.

edge.rationale: Trigonometric ratios require naming side relationships relative to the chosen angle.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes ratios using the wrong sides.

edge.rationale: Choosing a trigonometric ratio requires knowing which side pairs each ratio connects.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot choose sine, cosine or tangent from known and unknown sides.

edge.rationale: Solving for a missing side requires selecting and applying the appropriate ratio.
edge.failure_signal: Learner chooses a ratio but cannot set up or solve the equation.

edge.rationale: Solving for an angle requires selecting a ratio and using inverse trigonometry.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses direct trig functions instead of inverse functions for angles.
